steps.say: Cryoglobulins solidify in the cold and melt on warming. Blood for testing is kept at body temperature until clotting finishes. Room temperature transport is the dissolver of the evidence. The laboratory is warned before sampling.
steps.tx: **Cryoglobulins** (cold-precipitating immunoglobulins) precipitate below **37 degrees** Celsius and redissolve on warming, tested in serum kept strictly at 37 degrees until clot separation. Cold **agglutinins** (cold red cell antibodies) spare serum testing. Purpura in the cold with a negative room-temperature sample indicates repeat testing with a pre-warmed 37-degree flask.

steps.say: Brouet type I is monoclonal from lymphoma or myeloma while mixed types II and III carry rheumatoid factor activity. Hepatitis C is the driver of mixed disease in Southern Europe. Typing with infection screens decides therapy.
steps.tx: One clone or many decides the Brouet label: type I carries a single monoclonal **IgM**, IgG, or IgA from lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, myeloma, or MGUS, while mixed II and III blend monoclonal or polyclonal **IgM** (rheumatoid factor active) against polyclonal IgG. Southern European mixed disease traces to chronic **hepatitis C**, with hepatitis B, HIV, SLE, Sjogren, and B-cell lymphoma behind the rest. Typing with infection screens indicates antivirals versus chemotherapy.

steps.say: The Meltzer triad of purpura with joint pains and weakness is the marker of mixed vasculitis. Palpable purpura with ulcers and Raynaud are present in the full skin picture. Triad with low C4 and rheumatoid factor is mixed cryoglobulinaemia.
steps.tx: **Meltzer triad** (purpura with arthralgias and weakness) marks mixed cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis, with palpable **purpura** (raised bleeding spots), leg ulcers, and Raynaud phenomenon. Painful sensory neuropathy or mononeuritis multiplex reaches up to **60 percent**, and skin biopsy shows leukocytoclastic venule vasculitis. Triad with low **C4** and rheumatoid factor positivity indicates mixed cryoglobulinaemia.

vis.alt: Palpable purpura on lower limbs with leukocytoclastic vasculitis on skin biopsy.
vis.caption: Palpable purpura with venule vasculitis marks mixed disease. Low C4 with rheumatoid factor confirms it. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Kidneys fail through membranoproliferative injury with IgM-kappa plugs under endothelium. Nephritic or nephrotic presentations both occur. Low C4 with rheumatoid factor points to the cause. Renal biopsy with cryoglobulin testing settles it.
steps.tx: Renal disease is type I membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (**MPGN**, tram-tracked glomeruli) with subendothelial **IgM-kappa** deposits, presenting nephritic (blood with hypertension) or nephrotic (heavy proteinuria) with low **C4** and rheumatoid factor positivity. Proteinuria with purpura and low C4 indicates cryoglobulinaemic MPGN. Renal biopsy with cryoglobulin testing settles the cause.

vis.alt: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis with tram-tracking and subendothelial immune deposits.
vis.caption: Tram-tracked glomeruli with IgM-kappa plugs define cryoglobulinaemic kidney injury. Low C4 points to the cause. Credit: Nephron.

steps.say: Type I disease is the clogger of small vessels with hyperviscosity. Headache with blurred vision and sausage veins are the markers of it. Deafness with digital ischaemia are present in the full picture. Emergency plasmapheresis is the clearer of the sludge.
steps.tx: Type I hyperviscosity (**hyperviscosity**, thick protein-clogged blood) gives headache, blurred vision with flame **hemorrhages** and venous **sausaging** (beaded retinal veins), deafness, and digital ischemia. **Plasmapheresis** (plasma exchange) is emergency therapy for hyperviscosity, clearing monoclonal protein within hours. Blurred vision with sausage veins in myeloma indicates urgent exchange.

steps.say: Direct antivirals are the cure of the hepatitis C driver in 12 weeks or less. Sofosbuvir with velpatasvir or glecaprevir with pibrentasvir are the clearers of the virus. Rituximab covers vasculitic flares during clearance. Cure of virus is cure of vasculitis.
steps.tx: Direct-acting antivirals (**DAAs**, hepatitis C cures) erase the driver: **sofosbuvir**-velpatasvir across **12 weeks**, or **glecaprevir**-pibrentasvir across **8 to 12 weeks**. **Rituximab** (anti-CD20) covers vasculitic flares during viral clearance. DAA is delayed only in severe vasculitis needing immediate immunosuppression. Viral cure is vasculitis cure.

steps.say: HCV-negative vasculitis takes steroids with rituximab 375 mg per square meter weekly for 4 weeks. Dosing follows body surface. Flares are retreated with repeat courses. Lymphoma or autoimmunity is sought as the alternate driver.
steps.tx: HCV-negative mixed vasculitis takes glucocorticoids with **rituximab at 375 mg** per square meter each week across **4 weeks**, dosed to body surface area. Repeat courses retreat flares. B-cell lymphoma with SLE or Sjogren is sought as the alternate driver when hepatitis screens stay negative.

steps.say: Cold purpura with arthralgias is tested warm, typed by Brouet, and traced to hepatitis C first. Kidneys are MPGN with low C4 while eyes are sausage veins in type I. Drivers are cured with antivirals or clone therapy. Warm sampling is never skipped.
steps.tx: Cold purpura with arthralgias and weakness is sampled warm at **37 degrees**, typed I versus mixed II and III, and traced to **hepatitis C** first. Kidneys show **MPGN** with low **C4** while type I eyes show venous **sausaging**. **DAAs** across **8 to 12 weeks** or **rituximab 375 mg** per square meter across **4 weeks** erase the driver. Warm sampling is never skipped.
